audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Neeko level 1 and level 6 and gave Renekton both post-item stages, which inverts the real shape of the lane on five of seven rows.
audit.why: Renekton is at 56.14% over 1035 games because he owns levels 1-5 outright — Neeko is squishy, has no dash outside her ult, and cannot escape E-W-Q. The page's own whys[5] and whys[6] say her Lost Chapter/Liandry's spike and full AP build are where she takes over. The Neeko-side mirror already set the chart to Renekton x4, Skill, Neeko, Neeko.
audit.corrected: Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Skill, Neeko, Neeko in both layers as one atomic group, ratings moved with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as Renekton's 'absolute peak' with no acknowledgement that Pop Blossom arrives at the same level.
audit.why: Pop Blossom is 120/105/90s and knocks up, then stuns, and its preparation is hidden while she is disguised — that is a real level-6 spike on her side, not a stage Renekton simply owns.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now says Dominus Fury chains stuns through her wind-up but her R lands the same level, so 6 turns on who commits first.
sources: kit: Pop Blossom text and cd

audit.why: The interactions on the page are real and correctly named: empowered W at 50+ Fury is a point-and-click 1.5s stun she cannot dodge or dash out of, Pop Blossom's preparation cannot complete through it, and Shapesplitter's clone baits a wasted E. Cooldowns were absent, so Tangle-Barbs' 12s at rank 1 is now stated where the player needs it.
audit.corrected: Cooldown number added to the do's and to Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every long content field is written in the FIRST person — 'I play patient', 'my Q-heal', 'I force all-in' — while the rest of the site speaks to the player in the second person.
audit.why: It reads as a different author mid-page and breaks the coaching voice the user approved.
audit.corrected: early, mid, late and whys[3] converted to second person at the same length; the typo 'dahing' is fixed to 'dashing' in the same pass.

edits.before: Dominus HP buffer absorbs her Pop Blossom burst and accelerates Fury for two back-to-back empowered W-stuns, stripping her of the channel she needs to kill me.
edits.after: Dominus Fury generation chains empowered W-stuns through her Pop Blossom wind-up, but her R lands the same level, so 6 turns on who commits first.

edits.before: She has no mobility through Levels 4-5 and my Q-heal erases her Q poke; I force all-in on every Fury-stocked window.
edits.after: She has no mobility through Levels 4-5 and your Q-heal erases her Q poke; force the all-in on every Fury-stocked window.

edits.before: Neeko wastes Tangle-Barbs — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Tangle-Barbs is 12s at rank 1 — bait it, then E-W-Q in that window.

edits.before: Track Neeko's Tangle-Barbs: Her root — extends through targets. Dodge it. When it is down — Fury W-stun + dash out.
edits.after: Tangle-Barbs roots and grows through each target it passes, 12s at rank 1 — dodge it, then Fury W-stun and dash out.

edits.before: Level 1 I play patient — no dash means I cannot run her down yet, and she has Blooming Burst (Q) re-blooms to poke at range, so I last-hit at max Q distance and refuse to eat chip damage for free. Level 2 changes everything: the moment I have E and W I look for an immediate all-in. She has no dash, so I E through her, land the empowered W two-hit stun, and Q-heal through any damage she threatens back before the root expires. She cannot channel Pop Blossom while she is stunned, which means my whole kit strips her only big cooldown of its setup. At Level 3 all three abilities are online and I keep pressing — if she tries to throw Tangle-Barbs (E) as a poke I step sideways and E in the instant the projectile passes, denying the root and landing W before she has any follow-up.
edits.after: Level 1 you play patient — no dash means you cannot run her down yet, and Blooming Burst (Q) re-blooms to poke at range, so last-hit at max Q distance and refuse to eat chip damage for free. At Level 3 all three abilities are online and you keep pressing — if she throws Tangle-Barbs (E) as a poke, step sideways and E in the instant the projectile passes, denying the root and landing W before she has any follow-up.

edits.before: Through Levels 4-5 I keep the tempo: my Q-heal sustains through her Q poke, and every time she walks up to last-hit I re-run the E-W-Q combo off a stocked Fury bar. The one thing I respect is her W-Shapesplitter clone — if she goes invisible I back off two steps and let her reappear before I dash in, because dahing into a gap where the real Neeko already walked away just burns my E with no target. Level 6 is my absolute peak: Dominus (R) gives me a fat HP buffer and floods me with Fury so I can chain two empowered W-stuns back-to-back. Pop Blossom (her R) has a long channel wind-up and I ignore it entirely — I walk through the storm while Dominus is active, land the first empowered W, and by the time that stun ends I have Fury for a second. She cannot finish the channel through two consecutive stuns and the Dominus HP means her single rotation does not finish me.

Level 6 is your peak: Dominus (R) gives you a fat HP buffer and floods you with Fury so you can chain two empowered W-stuns back-to-back. Pop Blossom is a 90-120s cooldown with a wind-up — walk through it while Dominus is active, land the first empowered W, and by the time that stun ends you have Fury for a second. She cannot finish the channel through two consecutive stuns.

edits.before: This is where the 56.14% starts to look closer. Neeko's Lost Chapter into Liandry's lands around the time Dominus cooldown normalises, and now a fully-set-up E-into-Pop Blossom unseen (she will walk it in under Shapesplitter invisibility or a disguise) is a one-shot on a squishy melee. I never facecheck fog in a sidelane once she has first item — that is exactly the angle where she channels Pop Blossom from a disguise and I die before I can E-dash the gap. Two items is full threat: keep fights in groups where my E-W-Q burst still lands on her before she completes the channel, and use the fact that she commits a long ult animation to close the gap and stun her mid-cast. She out-scales in isolated picks, but in the 5v5 she is still squishy and I am still point-and-click W.
edits.after: This is where the 56.14% starts to look closer. Never facecheck fog in a sidelane once she has first item — that is exactly the angle where she opens Pop Blossom from a disguise, and its preparation is hidden while she is disguised. Two items is full threat: keep fights in groups where your E-W-Q burst still lands before she completes the cast, and use her long ult animation to close the gap and stun her mid-cast. She wins isolated picks, but in the 5v5 she is squishy and your W is point-and-click.

notes: The packet suspectName 'Use Shapesplitter' in wants.foe[1] is a FALSE POSITIVE — Shapesplitter is Neeko's real W name and the line uses it correctly. The five chart rows are proposed as matched full/content pairs in one group and match both the packet and the already-audited Neeko side. Two of the packet defects are now addressed: the sequencing gap (Tangle-Barbs 12s at rank 1 is named as the window to engage in) and the first-person voice throughout early/mid/late. The mirror's own note flags that its 36.36%-over-22-games sample sits oddly against giving Neeko both item stages; that concern does not apply here, where the sample is 1035 games.
